title: Storage Optimization
description: Optimize your SSD performance, manage storage efficiently, and maintain your drives for maximum longevity and speed.

steps.title: SSD Health & Performance Basics
steps.content:
Understanding your SSD for optimal performance:

**Check SSD Health:**
Use CrystalDiskInfo to monitor:
• Health Status (Good/Caution/Bad)
• Temperature
• Total Host Writes (TBW remaining)
• Power On Hours

**NVMe vs SATA Performance:**
• NVMe: Up to 7000+ MB/s read/write
• SATA: Up to 550 MB/s read/write
Your OMEN likely has NVMe for the OS drive

**Temperature Guidelines:**
• Normal: 30-50°C
• Under load: 50-70°C
• Throttling: 70°C+

infoBox.title: SSD Lifespan
infoBox.content: Modern SSDs typically last 5-10 years with normal use. Check TBW (Terabytes Written) rating - most users never reach this limit.

steps.title: Windows Storage Settings
steps.content:
Optimize Windows settings for SSD performance:

**Enable TRIM (Usually automatic):**
1. Open Command Prompt as Admin
2. Run: fsutil behavior query DisableDeleteNotify
3. If result is 0, TRIM is enabled
4. If 1, enable with: fsutil behavior set DisableDeleteNotify 0

**Disable Disk Defragmentation for SSDs:**
1. Search "Defragment and Optimize Drives"
2. Select your SSD
3. Click "Change settings"
4. Ensure "Optimize" is set, not "Defragment"
Note: Windows 10/11 automatically optimizes SSDs (TRIM), not defragment

**Disable Superfetch/SysMain (Optional):**
1. Press Win + R, type services.msc
2. Find "SysMain"
3. Right-click → Properties → Stop
4. Set Startup type to Disabled
Note: This is optional and may not noticeably improve modern SSDs

infoBox.title: Don't Defragment SSDs
infoBox.content: Traditional defragmentation is harmful to SSDs and unnecessary. Windows automatically uses TRIM instead, which is the correct optimization for SSDs.

steps.title: Storage Cleanup & Maintenance
steps.content:
Keep your SSD clean for best performance:

**Disk Cleanup:**
1. Win + R → cleanmgr
2. Select drive → OK
3. Click "Clean up system files"
4. Select:
• Windows Update Cleanup
• Previous Windows installations
• Temporary files
• Thumbnails

**Storage Sense (Automatic):**
1. Settings → System → Storage
2. Enable Storage Sense
3. Configure:
• Run during low disk space
• Delete temp files older than 1 day
• Delete Recycle Bin items older than 30 days

**Clear Browser Cache:**
Browsers can accumulate GBs of cache data
Chrome: Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data
Firefox: Settings → Privacy → Clear Data
Edge: Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data

steps.title: Game Storage Management
steps.content:
Optimize storage for gaming:

**Install Games on Fast Drive:**
• Install competitive/frequently played games on NVMe SSD
• Move older/casual games to secondary storage
• Steam: Settings → Downloads → Steam Library Folders
• Epic: Settings → Manage Games → Install Location

**Move Game Libraries:**
**Steam:**
1. Create new library folder on target drive
2. Right-click game → Properties → Local Files
3. Move Install Folder → Select new location

**Epic Games:**
1. Move folder manually to new location
2. Uninstall from Epic (keep files)
3. Reinstall and point to moved folder

**DirectStorage:**
Windows 11 feature for faster game loading
Requirements: NVMe SSD, DirectX 12, supported game
Enable: Games automatically use when available

infoBox.title: Performance Tip
infoBox.content: Keep 10-20% of your SSD free for optimal performance. SSDs slow down significantly when nearly full due to how they write data.

steps.title: Advanced Storage Tips
steps.content:
Advanced optimization techniques:

**Page File Optimization:**
1. System Properties → Advanced → Performance Settings
2. Advanced tab → Virtual Memory → Change
3. For SSDs: System managed or fixed size
4. Recommended: 1.5x RAM if you have space

**Disable Hibernation (Save Space):**
1. Open Command Prompt as Admin
2. Run: powercfg -h off
3. Frees up RAM-sized space (8-32GB)
Note: Disables hybrid sleep/fast startup

**Move User Folders:**
Move large folders (Downloads, Videos) to secondary drive:
1. Right-click folder in File Explorer
2. Properties → Location tab
3. Move to new location

**Symbolic Links:**
For apps that don't support custom install locations:
mklink /D "C:\OriginalPath" "D:\NewPath"

infoBox.title: SSD Over-Provisioning
infoBox.content: Leaving 10% of SSD unpartitioned can improve performance and lifespan. This space is used for wear leveling and garbage collection.
